description:
CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became (util.DateUtilityJob) and reached as a plain object: no EXEC PGM= anywhere in app/jcl or app/proc names it, and it is CALLed four times from two online programs - CORPT00C at L392 and L412, COTRN02C at L393 and L413 - so there is no JobLauncher, no job repository and no HTTP layer between this assertion and the bytes it asserts on. LS-DATE='ABCD-EF-GH' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-DD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85), each written out to the declared PIC X(10) width because the declared width itself changes the outcome; LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the entire output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. The program declares no ENVIRONMENT DIVISION, no FILE-CONTROL, no SELECT and no FD - only WORKING-STORAGE (L22) and LINKAGE (L83) - so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and leaves no final state to state. It declares no job parameter either, and not merely because no JCL step reaches it: ParityCase refuses a job parameter on any unitKind but BATCH_JOB, since a value parked among the inputs would be fed back into the unit and then compared against itself. Its whole observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE, which is 3 here and stays 3 rather than being normalised to the 4, 8 or 12 a batch step would carry. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of the thirteen spans of 01 WS-MESSAGE (L42-L57), whose widths sum mechanically to 4+11+4+1+15+1+9+10+1+10+10+1+3 = exactly 80, and are never captured from a COBOL run: no Language Environment CEE* service exists in this environment, so the CALL to CEEDAYS at L116 cannot be executed at all. The pinned site is L143-L144, arm 8 of the ten-arm EVALUATE TRUE (L128-L149, WHEN OTHER last at L147-L148): FC-NON-NUMERIC-DATA is matched at L143 and moves 'Nonnumeric data' at L144. Because EVALUATE selects the FIRST matching WHEN, this arm sits ahead of arm 9 and ahead of WHEN OTHER, and any reordering that let the default precede it would break the case. That literal is already exactly fifteen characters, so it fills WS-RESULT X(15) with no padding added by the author and none added by the MOVE - unlike the author-padded 'Bad Pic String ' or 'YearInEra is 0 ' - and it is reproduced byte for byte, run-together capitalisation included, rather than re-spelt as 'Non-numeric data' or 'Nonnumeric  data'. Severity 3 and message 2520 are DECODED from the halfwords 0x0003 and 0x09D8 of the 88-level VALUE X'000309D859C3C5C5' at L69 - 0x09D8 is 9*256+216 - with the trailing 0x59 case-severity byte and the 0xC3C5C5 facility bytes that spell 'CEE' in EBCDIC left where they are; the number is never interpolated from the neighbouring arms, because L68 carries 2518 and L70 carries 2521, so 2519 does not exist and the nine numbers are non-contiguous throughout. Every numeric position of the date holds a letter while the delimiters still line up, and that is what separates 2520 from the arms it is most easily confused with: the picture string is well formed, so this is not the 2518 FC-BAD-PIC-STRING that a damaged mask produces; the field is full rather than short, so it is not the 2507 FC-INSUFFICIENT-DATA a truncated mask produces; and the defect is the field's contents rather than a numeric value out of range, so it is neither the 2517 FC-INVALID-MONTH the month cases drive (case12 from the zero month in '2022-00-15' and case13 from '2022-13-15') nor the 2521 FC-YEAR-IN-ERA-ZERO the same guard chain reports for the zero-year date the LINKAGE table runs case20 with. case19 is this arm's other case and reaches it from ten blanks, where here the ten positions are filled but alphabetic; the pair is what stops a validator that tests only for emptiness, or only for the presence of a digit, from passing both. Because 2520 is neither the '0000' that lets a caller continue nor the '2513' both callers single out and tolerate, CORPT00C (L396-L406) and COTRN02C (L397-L407) each treat this result as a hard error and paint their 'Not a valid date' message. The TstDate span carries an expected corruption rather than a defect to repair: L105-L106 moves LENGTH OF LS-DATE, always the declared ten, into the S9(4) BINARY Vstring-length of WS-DATE-TO-TEST, and the group move at L122 then overwrites the clean date L107-L108 had placed in WS-DATE with the leftmost ten bytes of that group, so WS-DATE keeps the two-byte halfword and only the first eight characters - 'ABCD-EF-' - while the trailing 'GH' falls off the end. The two halfword bytes 0x00 and 0x0A are BINARY and are written here as the explicit escapes \u0000 and \u000A rather than as an implicit newline escape, and no position of this case's echoed span holds a character zero, which is precisely the binary-versus-character distinction the zero-year date forces and this alphabetic one does not. WS-DATE-FMT is set once at L111-L113 before the CALL and L122 targets WS-DATE alone, so the mask span stays clean and echoes YYYY-MM-DD in full. Every byte below is US-ASCII, the code page of the fixtures, never a platform default.

THE TWO CALL PARAMETERS, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. unitStimulus.linkage carries this case's whole input: LS-DATE = 'ABCD-EF-GH' and LS-DATE-FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD', each written out to the ten characters PIC X(10) declares at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:84-85 with every trailing space visible - a mask longer than ten characters is TRUNCATED by the receiving field, and the truncation changes the message number, so the width has to be readable at the point the value is written. CSUTLDTC seeds no dataset and drives no screen, so these two values are the only thing a case varies; they used to live in a table in CSUTLDTCParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', which meant this file stated an eighty-byte result with nothing in it to say what was validated, and cases that differ only in their input were indistinguishable on disk.
